helpful: The statpack's per-Term federal-band segment table gave a clean, leakage-safe anchor for the arrival-moment federal-petitioner class
Provisioned petition.txt and questions-presented.txt were high-quality and made the QP and the warrants-review posture directly readable
gaps: No sanctioned way to see a related SCOTUS docket's state (the President's companion petition): RECAP search carries no SCOTUS dockets, so coordination signals between companion petitions are invisible at arrival
The corpus citation filter is a known-case lookup over sparse coverage (161 of ~590k scotus rows), so pulling topical priors like Osborn v. Haley by cite is rarely productive
notes: The single fedcourts query cost 1329 ranged GETs / ~348 MB and exceeded a 120s foreground timeout before returning an empty coverage-gap result; a cheaper failure mode for sparse filters would help arrival cells stay inside budget.
